thesisQuality.note: Commercial driverless operations, fully allocated planned capacity and customer negotiations support a strong band, but durable value capture/unit economics remain unproven.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Revenue is growing from a tiny base but Q2 revenue was $2M against $266M operating loss and ~$225M operating cash use; liquidity near $1.2B supports execution but dilution is active.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: ~$12.64B market cap on Sep. 18 is demanding versus $14M-$16M 2026 revenue guidance and unproven scaled margins, placing valuation in the weak band.

catalystScore.note: 200+ driverless-truck year-end target, planned manufacturing scale and 2027 DaaS negotiations provide multiple identifiable catalysts, though execution remains future-dated.

governancePower.note: Management has disclosed explicit operating/cash targets and funded scaling, but repeated ATM issuance and still-unproven economics constrain a higher governance/capital-allocation assessment.

alignment2036.note: Autonomous freight directly addresses logistics availability, safety and infrastructure efficiency; commercial driverless deployment makes this more than conceptual exposure.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Aurora Driver is designed as a reusable autonomy platform and current trucking deployment spans multiple customer relationships, but present economics remain concentrated in trucking scale-up.

bottleneckControl.note: Validated driverless autonomy and integrated second-generation hardware are meaningful constrained capabilities, but manufacturing, operations, regulation and economics remain successor bottlenecks outside Aurora's sole control.

scenarioRobustness.note: Liquidity and multiple commercial partners provide resilience, but the thesis remains materially dependent on autonomous-trucking adoption, manufacturing scale and regulatory acceptance.

substitutionResilience.note: Driverless commercial miles and integrated hardware/software create qualification and execution barriers, but competing autonomy stacks and conventional freight remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.note: Industrial partnerships and second-generation fleet manufacturing support scale, but current evidence does not establish broad supplier redundancy or tested contingency paths.

pricingPower.note: Capacity allocation signals demand, but current revenue is small and scaled DaaS gross margins/contract economics are not yet demonstrated, so durable pricing power remains unproven.

risk.note: High cash burn, ATM dilution, back-end-loaded revenue and unproven scaled unit economics create substantial execution/downside risk despite strong liquidity.

confidence.note: Core operating and financial facts are primary-source addressed and current valuation has an independent market source; confidence is reduced because most operating claims share one issuer origin and key scaled economics remain unknown.

thesis: Aurora has crossed from autonomy development into commercial driverless trucking scale-up, giving it credible exposure to a durable logistics bottleneck, but the investment case still requires successful manufacturing/deployment scale and eventual DaaS economics.
keyRisk: Capital-intensive scaling, dilution and a demanding valuation can overwhelm technical progress if fleet growth, utilization or gross-margin milestones slip.
nextCatalyst: Execution against the planned 1,000-truck annual manufacturing run-rate and more than 200 driverless trucks in operation by year-end 2026.

scoreBreakdown.note: earthScore records the methodology-weighted component base; risk and confidence are separately source-addressed for runtime methodology treatment.
